audits.summary: The local sidebar is structurally close to the original classic Code sidebar. Ported pieces with source citations include: row and group geometry and tokens, the Filter menu, the single and multi session row menus with letter hotkeys, multi-select, nested lineage runs, 20-row truncation, the empty and loading states, the resize handle, the New row and the account footer. The remaining gaps are mostly behaviour, not pixels. A session that finishes a turn in the background never becomes unread. Folder grouping uses the raw cwd instead of the repo, and there is no 'Other' bucket. These are all missing: the collapsed-sidebar hover peek, the ⌘1–9 jump keys with hold-⌘ number hints, right-click menus on group headers, drag and drop, and the ⇧⌘K search palette. Smaller polish gaps remain in status-glyph tooltips, the 'Open in' submenu, and inline rename and action feedback.

The titlebar inside the window is a close port of the original, and each piece cites its source line: origin glyph, rename button and input, folder pill with tooltip, Changes toggle with its activity dot, kebab, What's new and the collapsed Back/Forward nav. The large remaining gaps are all in the Electron shell around it. Closing the window quits the app (the original hides it), no native right-click edit menu exists, and the app menu is a skeleton: no File or Help menu, no Edit > Find, no View pane items, and the Go menu has no Previous/Next Session or Search…. Window size and position are never saved, and the native window chrome ignores the app's theme. Two notes outside this region: the collapsed-sidebar hover peek with its 28px trigger is also missing (likely the sidebar region's), and local comments cite index.chunk-D6ATlqeD.js, but the current bundle is reference/current-2.2553.1/asar/.vite/build/index.chunk-ChZ67Jhw.js.

Structurally the home page is very close to the original. The greeting, the stats card geometry (6 tiles, 26-week heatmap, Overview/Models plus All/30d/7d tabs, the Models chart and list, the book footnote), the Action Center and the pet all line up with code-home-current.png to within about a pixel once you allow for its 0.9 scale. What remains is mostly data and chrome. The stats come from a forward-only in-app ledger mixed with account/usage token buckets, so the card can show Sessions 0, Messages 0, Peak hour — next to Total tokens 9.9M. A non-original provenance footer sits under the card on every home view, and a "Connecting to DeepSeek…" card shows on every launch. The environment chips' folder and branch pickers are simplified custom menus with native title tooltips instead of the original's Recent picker, searchable branch combobox and CDS tooltips. The polish gaps are the skeleton, the tab hover and the chart tooltip.

The composer is structurally and visually close to the original. The CDS card and chin geometry, the send/stop crossfade, the context ring, the chin chord shortcuts, the Mode/Model/Effort popups, the slash menu geometry, the ProseMirror command chips and the "History i/n" strip are all ported, each citing its source. What remains is mostly behaviour. Switching sessions throws away the unsent draft. Skills cannot be found or typed through "/", and choosing one from the Add menu puts a pill in the attachments row instead of an inline chip. The editor and the Mode/Model/Effort controls are disabled while a turn runs or a session loads, where the original keeps them usable. Escape stops a running turn only when the editor has focus, and @-mentions stay as plain text instead of chips. The Mode menu still lacks Accept edits and the "Default" badge. The two deferred history features are still missing (Ctrl+R search, ↑ on an empty editor to pull back the last queued message), and the Send, Stop and Model buttons have different accessible names.

The transcript is close to the original at the row level. Assistant Markdown (links, tables, math, footnotes, reveal), the code-block shell and copy button, user bubbles (chips, slash pill, collapse, attachments), the turn footer and user Copy/timestamp, error cards and markers, and the follow/restore scroll controller are all ported carefully, each citing the original. The largest gaps that remain sit above the individual rows. Syntax highlighting covers only 5 grammars, where the original bundles 235. The jump control is the round chat-chrome button with an instant jump, but the official screenshot shows the compact CaretDown chip, which scrolls smoothly. There is no right-click menu in the transcript and no Cmd+F find bar. The feed/article keyboard and screen-reader structure is also missing. Smaller polish gaps are secret redaction in code, how a failed send is shown, and triple-click selecting a whole code block.

This region is close to the original. The classic tool rows, tool-group summaries and expansion, command `$`/output/running-footer bodies, Read/Edit in-card layouts, approval-card actions, hotkey arming and the question-card pager/Skip/Other all port the cited modules closely, and the live DeepSeek screenshots match the source structure. The biggest remaining gap is the file-change approval card. It embeds a local `FileChanges` block (a Changes-pane diff with a broken icon/path/kind row) in place of the original layout: the full path in a detail box, then the in-card Edit/Write diff body. Other gaps are mostly in how DeepSeek-specific data is shown: subagent row labels, the "Asked" row body, multi-select questions, plus the missing 1px `epitaxy-diff` ring under the default Claude code themes and a few approval-card extras or omissions.

The pane chrome is close to 2.2553.1. That covers the tile engine (drop zones, separators, arrange popup, Fill/Tile, popout), the pane controls, the Files tree keyboard model and states, the tab look and tooltips, and the Changes diff renderer (sticky file headers, header menu, hunk separators, context expansion, split and wrap, Collapse/Expand all). The biggest remaining gaps are inside the panes. The Files viewer is a plain unnumbered, unhighlighted <pre> under an invented 11px "← path" row. A failed open shows raw Electron IPC error text. The Changes header has neither the "Show files" list toggle (⌘⇧Y) nor the diff-scope picker; it is a static bold "Uncommitted changes". Smaller gaps follow: tab overflow and preview-tab order, file context menus, the missing Terminal pane, header title styling, and the two diff display toggles. Two more were not ranked: the tree filter's "? for contents" content search (panes-tile-current.js:4434, :4669, :5817-5914) and the "Preview tabs" setting (:6905-6915). All local citations were checked against the current code. B12 (Plan list, thinking rows) was excluded, and fixes that touch source-session.jsx should be rebased after B12 lands.

The neutral git band is structurally close to the original. Row tokens (40px/8px/5px gap/10px radius/alpha-1), the repo and branch chips with the 16-char head/tail split, CDS tooltips, the disabled-reason wrapper, the exact Commit turn text and the polling cadence all match. The remaining gaps are mostly behavioral and visual. The local diff scope is HEAD to working tree, while the original compares against the merge-base with the default branch and only enables Commit when the working tree is dirty. Commit and the +N −M counts are painted as ghost text instead of CDS secondary buttons. Local shows a Dismiss button that commit mode never has, and the band pops in and out on every session switch instead of holding a stale snapshot. Smaller copy and alignment slips remain in the chip menus. The rail layout still exists only as an unmounted fixture.

The Customize list pages are already close to 2.2553.1. They match on the page-shell header with the collapsible CDS search, the fixed CDS table with the original column widths and row geometry, the loading skeletons, the 'Couldn’t load …' blocks, the skill and plugin drill-ins, and the 'stopped working' card. Most remaining gaps are in the detail and empty views. The skill detail header uses its own controls instead of the Try in chat / Switch / ⋮ actions and the Added by / Last updated facts. Connector details still open in a 280px side card instead of the page-shell drill-in. Empty states have no pictogram and are not vertically centred. There are also several local-only additions: notice paragraphs at the top of each page, the marketplace name next to every plugin, the 'MCP server · N tools' Type cell, and no 'Filter by status' control. I checked every finding against the current source and the latest local screenshots (work/deepseek-live-20261001/b07-*/s-*.png and analysis/batch-20260920/skills-mcp-ui-2026-10-01T17-30-20.013Z/*.png).

The settings region is close to the original. The shell geometry and animation, nav groups, search ranking and highlighting, the row/group layout (Av/Fv), switches, segments and selects, the Code appearance grid, Local sessions rows, the Developer two-pane view and the Storage meter are all ported with source citations and look right in the latest screenshots. What remains is mostly behavior: opening Settings does not focus Search, the Usage page mixes two original variants so the nav can disappear, first-run defaults for notifications and keep-awake are reversed, and every save briefly disables the whole page. The other gaps are the deferred Storage report content (raw folders instead of the original areas and kinds) and some low-severity copy, accessibility and visual polish.

The core shared primitives are close ports of the original: SourceMenu (Base UI menu: layering, positioner, highlight/typeahead, close-reason focus return, submenu safe polygon), SourceTooltip, SourceSelect and the Toast stack all follow the 2.2553.1 source closely. The remaining gaps are mostly places that skip those primitives. There is no native Electron text context menu. Two focus-ring tokens (--cds-focus-color, --cds-border-focus) and one button-text token (--cds-text-on-primary) are used but never defined, so icon buttons get no keyboard focus ring and the Save/Archive all buttons in the sidebar dialogs have invisible labels. Six live menus and popovers still run on the old code-ui Popover/MenuItem. Dialogs are hand-rolled instead of using the CDS Dialog/AlertDialog. Slash-command notices and errors appear as inline banners instead of toasts. The Keyboard shortcuts dialog is a 6-row stub with no ⌘/ shortcut. A global Escape handler closes every open surface at once, and shortcut glyphs are pre-formatted with the wrong modifier order.

The token layer itself matches the original. app/index.html loads design-system.css (c6a992d55), desktop-layout.css (shared-styles) and shared-frame.css, and they are byte-identical to the 2.2553.1 bundle apart from the /assets/v1 to ./ URL rewrite. That means every token value, the light/dark palettes, the @font-face rules and all 19 woff2 fonts (in app/public/assets/v1) come from the original. The drift sits in the local glue code. No CDS root sets data-platform, and the sidebar is not a cds-root at all. About 15 token names that do not exist are referenced; some have no fallback, so they silently remove focus rings and turn one button label invisible. Dialog and popover surfaces are hand-styled instead of using the CDS tokens. On top of that there is a font-stack override, theme handling that ignores nativeTheme, the system default and the dark window background, and a blanket reduced-motion kill used instead of the original data-reduce-motion attribute.

findings.title: A session that finishes a turn in the background never becomes unread (no accent 'Unread response' dot)
findings.difference: In the original, a code session that finishes a turn while you are not viewing it has state 'ready'. Its leading slot then shows the accent status-dot with the label 'Unread response', and its row menu offers 'Mark as read'. Opening the session clears it. Locally, sessionMetadata.unread is only set by the manual 'Mark as unread' item. The turn/completed handler only refreshes the session. So a session that finished in the background looks identical to an idle one. The Home attention list ('unread' kind) also never fills automatically. Separately, the local CSS turns the title of an unread row text-primary. The original row has no unread title style. That rule only shows today when a row is marked unread by hand, but it would become a visible difference once unread is set automatically.

Unread row styles: sidebar-rows.js:7143-7180 kD and 7520-7540 ND have no unread title class. Local: app/src/main.jsx:853 (turn/completed only calls refreshSession and loadQueue). app/src/main.jsx:1076 (navigate clears unread). app/src/main.jsx:1553-1554 (the only place unread is set). app/src/home-model.mjs:33-42 (Home attention depends on meta.unread). app/src/source-sidebar.jsx:229-238 SessionStatus. app/src/source-sidebar.css:222 (local-only unread title colour).
findings.fix: Add a pure helper to app/src/sidebar-model.js, for example unreadOnTurnCompleted({threadId, currentId, knownIds, ownerOf}). It returns true when the thread is a sidebar row (not a sub-agent thread; ownerThreadId(state, id) === id), is in config.threadIds, and is not the open session (also when the window is unfocused/hidden, if desired). In app/src/main.jsx:853, when it returns true, call updateSessionMetadata(threadId, {unread: true}). Alternatively, set it in app/electron/main.cjs where the bridge notification passes, so the flag persists even if the renderer misses the event. Keep the clear on navigate (main.jsx:1076). Delete the local-only rule `.source-session-row[data-unread] .source-session-name { color: var(--cds-text-primary) }` in app/src/source-sidebar.css:222.
findings.verification: Unit test: cd app && node --test tests/sidebar-model.test.mjs, with new helper cases for the current session, a sub-agent thread, an unknown id and a background row. Offscreen suites 'sidebar' and 'home-page' (and 'sidebar-rest'): start a fixture turn in session B, switch to A before it completes, then assert B's leading slot has .status-dot[data-kind=ready] with role=status and aria-label 'Unread response', its row menu shows 'Mark as read', Home lists it as unread, and opening B clears all three.

findings.title: Folder grouping keys on the raw cwd; the original groups by repo, adds ' · disambiguation' to duplicate names and puts non-repo sessions in a final 'Other' group
findings.difference: The original 'Folder' grouping buckets code sessions by project identity. Repos with a remote are keyed by owner/name, so clones and worktrees of one repo merge. Local repos without a remote are keyed by cwd. Sessions with no repo info go into one 'Other' bucket appended after all projects. That bucket has no '+' button unless there is a prefill. Labels are project names, with ' · {disambiguationText}' added when two names collide. The reference screenshot shows 'Other' as the last group. Locally, every distinct cwd string becomes its own group, labelled with the folder basename and sorted by recency. Non-git folders each get their own group, worktrees of the same repo split apart, and two folders with the same basename show identical headers.
findings.evidence: Original: sidebar-groups.js:19580-19592 (bucket key = Vc(d) ?? _B). sidebar-groups.js:19555-19565 (label `${name} · ${disambiguationText}`). sidebar-groups.js:19640-19650 (the `project-__no_project__` bucket labelled zo.otherProjects is pushed after the project buckets). sidebar-session.js:20892-20903 IJ (owner/name, else cwd when no owner, else undefined). ion-dist/assets/v1/shared-2-C6aD8DvJ.js has otherProjects:{defaultMessage:'Other'}. sidebar-groups.js:19866-19880 (no '+' on the Other bucket without a prefill). analysis/pixel-reference/code-home-current.png ('Other' group last). Local: app/src/sidebar-model.js:227-244 (Map keyed by session.cwd || fallbackCwd, folderName label).
findings.fix: In app/electron/git-status.cjs and main.cjs, resolve and cache, per session cwd, {isRepo, toplevel, owner, name} from git rev-parse --show-toplevel and the parsed origin URL. Attach this to sessions as repoInfo, or send it as a cwd→repo map with the sidebar snapshot. In sidebar-model.js buildSidebarGroups (project branch), compute the key with IJ's rules: owner/name when there is an owner, otherwise the cwd for a repo without a remote, otherwise the special `__no_project__` key. Label repo buckets with the repo name and add ' · <parent folder>' when two labels collide. Append the 'Other' bucket after the sorted projects, and give it no cwd so no '+' renders.
findings.verification: Unit test: cd app && node --test tests/sidebar-model.test.mjs, with new cases covering a non-repo cwd going to 'Other' last, two worktrees sharing owner/name merging, a no-remote repo keyed by cwd, and duplicate basenames getting distinct labels. Offscreen 'sidebar' suite, using a fixture with one non-git folder: assert the last .source-group-heading text is 'Other' and that it has no 'New session in' button.

findings.title: Collapsed sidebar has no hover peek: hovering 'Show sidebar' should float the sidebar body as a card
findings.difference: In the original, when the sidebar is collapsed, hovering the 'Show sidebar' trigger (or a bridge zone) sets data-hovering and data-peeked on .dframe-root. The full sidebar body then appears as a floating card: 280px wide, max-height 70vh, padding 15.5px 7.5px 13px, card radius, --df-shadow-pop. It animates from opacity 0, translate(0,-6px) scale(.98) to none over .14s/.18s, and transitions only after the first peek. The trigger has aria-expanded and aria-controls and gets bg-neutral-30 while the peek is open. Escape closes the peek and refocuses the trigger. Locally, the collapsed aside is hidden outright (visibility hidden, width 0). The titlebar 'Show sidebar' button has no pointer-enter handler, no aria-expanded and no aria-controls, so switching sessions while collapsed means fully expanding the sidebar. HANDOFF 0.2.93 lists this as a deferred gap, and it is still missing.

Local: app/src/style.css:389-397 (.sidebar-collapsed .app-sidebar visibility hidden). app/src/source-titlebar.jsx:198-207 (ToolButton 'Show sidebar' with onClick only). app/src/main.jsx:2039 (the root uses a class, not data-collapsed). The loaded app/public/assets/v1/shared-styles-DunnEebG.css already contains the .dframe-peek-bridge/[data-hovering] rules.
findings.fix: Add peek state (hovering, peeked) in app/src/main.jsx, open on pointerenter of the titlebar 'Show sidebar' wrapper (as Nb/Ib do) and close on pointerleave of the trigger, bridge and body, with a short grace period. Mirror it to .dframe-root as data-hovering and data-peeked. Keep the aside mounted while collapsed, and make .dframe-sidebar-body the floating card. Either switch the collapsed root from the .sidebar-collapsed class to the data-collapsed attribute (the loaded shared-styles rules then apply; override the aside 'pill' layout for the local titlebar), or copy the :1415-1455 body and bridge rules under .sidebar-collapsed[data-hovering]. Add aria-expanded and aria-controls to the 'Show sidebar' ToolButton in app/src/source-titlebar.jsx. Escape closes the peek and refocuses the trigger. Opening a row from the peek closes it. Keep the resize handle hidden.
findings.verification: Offscreen suites 'titlebar' and 'sidebar-chrome': collapse with ⌘B, hover 'Show sidebar' and assert .dframe-sidebar-body is visible (opacity 1, width 280, height ≤ 70vh, box-shadow not none) and aria-expanded=true. Move the pointer away: the body is hidden. Hover again and press Escape: focus returns to 'Show sidebar'. Click a row in the peek: the session opens and the peek closes.

findings.title: ⌘1–9 session jump and the hold-⌘ (or Ctrl+Shift) number hints are missing
findings.difference: In the original, while the sidebar is visible, ⌘+Digit1–9 (no other modifiers, not a repeat, no palette open) scrolls to and clicks the Nth visible session row. Holding ⌘ alone (desktop) or Ctrl+Shift for 200ms shows small keycaps 1–9 over the leading slot of the first nine visible rows. The keycaps are not shown while focus is in an INPUT, TEXTAREA or SELECT. Ctrl+Shift+digit also jumps. The hints hide on key release, blur, visibilitychange, or a mouse move, click or wheel without the modifier. Locally, no ⌘/Ctrl digit handler exists anywhere in app/src or app/electron, and rows carry no data-jump-hint-row or data-row-key.

findings.fix: Create app/src/sidebar-jump-model.mjs with the oj/sj modifier predicates, the ij digit parser and the input-focus guard. In app/src/source-sidebar.jsx, add data-jump-hint-row and data-row-key to .source-session-row. Add a window keydown/keyup/blur/mousemove/mousedown/wheel/visibilitychange hook: Meta+1–9 (sidebar not collapsed, no menu or dialog open) calls scrollIntoView then .click() on the Nth visible [data-row-main-button]. Holding the modifier for 200ms renders aria-hidden <kbd> hints with mj's classes inside the first nine visible rows. Ctrl+Shift+digit jumps through the hint map.
findings.verification: Unit test: cd app && node --test tests/sidebar-jump-model.test.mjs (predicates, digit parsing from code/key, input guard). Offscreen 'sidebar-chrome' or 'sidebar' suite: press Meta+2 and the second visible row becomes current. Hold Meta for 250ms and kbd 1..n appear in the leading slots; release Meta and they disappear. With focus in the search INPUT no hints appear. Collapsed sidebar: Meta+1 does nothing.

findings.title: Group headers lack the original right-click menus; custom-group management uses a local ⋮ button, a dialog rename and an unconfirmed 'Remove group'
findings.difference: In the original, right-clicking a project group header opens a context menu: 'New session', a separator, then 'Move up', 'Move down' and 'Sort A to Z'. The project order is persisted and can be reset. Right-clicking a custom group header opens: 'New session', 'Rename group' (inline rename in the header), 'Change icon…', 'New group…', Move up/Move down/Sort A to Z, a separator, and 'Delete group' (danger). Delete opens a confirm dialog titled 'Delete group?' with the body '“{groupName}” will be removed. The # item(s) in it will no longer be grouped.' (or 'Nothing is in it.') and a 'Delete' button. An empty custom group shows 'Drag or move sessions here'. The New group dialog is a CDS dialog with placeholder 'Group name'. Its buttons are 'Cancel' and 'Create group', or 'Create and group by custom' with the note 'The list will switch to Custom groups to show it.' when you are not grouped by custom. Locally: the nav onContextMenu explicitly ignores .source-group-heading. Custom groups get a non-original DotsVertical 'More options for group X' button whose menu has 'Rename group' (modal dialog) and 'Remove group', which deletes immediately with no confirm. Project groups have no menu and no way to reorder. Every empty group says 'No active sessions'. The group dialog's submit button says 'Save'/'Saving…'.

findings.title: Session rows cannot be dragged (pin by drag, reorder pins, move into custom groups, reorder projects)
findings.difference: In the original, every session row is a drag source (.df-drag-shiftable, drag controller with a tear-off payload). Dropping it on the Pinned section pins it. While dragging, an empty Pinned area shows a 'Drag to pin' / 'Drop here' / 'Let go' target row with a Pin glyph that rotates and scales. The first pin made from the menu triggers the tip 'Tip: you can drag sessions here to pin them'. Pinned rows reorder by drag, with a .12s shift transition. Dropping onto a custom group shows an accent drop ring (bg-accent-muted ring-2 ring-inset ring-fill-accent), and dragging out offers 'Ungroup'. Project sections reorder by drag. During a drag the root carries data-session-dragging. Locally there is no row drag at all; the code comment at source-sidebar.jsx:823 says 'there is no row drag'. Pinning, moving to a group and reordering pins are only possible from menus.
findings.evidence: Original: sidebar-groups.js:16985-17013 (row drag start via ik() with the drag_tear_off payload). sidebar-groups.js:17202-17213 (row div 'relative df-drag-shiftable', opacity-50 while an assignment is pending). sidebar-groups.js:17529-17546 (custom-group drop ring). sidebar-main.js:9220-9250 SP/CP ('Drag to pin', 'Drop here', 'Let go', dragPinHint tip). sidebar-session-items.js:205-208 and sidebar-groups.js:8766 (maybeShowDragPinHint after pinning). sidebar-session.js:16068-16090 (sidebar_project_reorder_dnd). desktop-layout.css:1490-1570 (drop overlay, [data-pin-dragging] .df-drag-shiftable transition, [data-session-dragging]). Local: app/src/source-sidebar.jsx:797-842 (rows have no drag handlers), app/src/source-sidebar.jsx:823.

findings.title: Window size/position never persisted; default and minimum size differ (1468×852, min 760×580 vs 1200×800, min 600×400)
findings.difference: The original remembers the main window's bounds, maximized and full-screen state, and display. It saves on resize/move (debounced) and on close, and restores maximize/full screen on launch, starting from 1200×800 when nothing is saved. The window can shrink to 600×400, which lets the narrow-viewport layout (narrowViewportMaxWidth 700) appear. findings.fix: Port getCodeStats to the DeepSeek core. (1) In harness/packages/codex-app-server/src/usage.js, add foldSessionStats(events) next to foldSessionUsage, honouring the same session/end-seed inherited cut. Per local day it records: sessions (+1 on the day of the first user/message), messages (user/message + assistant/message, the activity.cjs:37 rule), toolCalls (tool/call), an hour histogram, and per-model tokens and usage keyed by assistant/message.data.message.source.model (usage.inputTokens + outputTokens; input/output/cacheRead). findings.title: Band counts, band visibility and Commit enablement use HEAD→worktree instead of merge-base with the default branch
findings.difference: The original band's diff stats (and the default Changes scope, 'All changes vs {base}') compare the working tree against merge-base(origin/<defaultBranch>, HEAD), plus untracked files. The row is visible when that diff has files. Commit is enabled only when the working tree itself is dirty (isWorkingTreeDirty); otherwise it is disabled with 'No changes to commit'. So after Claude commits on a feature branch, a worktree branch, or main with unpushed commits, the original band stays visible with +N −M for the whole branch and a disabled Commit. Locally `git diff HEAD` is used, so the band vanishes after every commit, the 'No changes to commit' state can never be reached, and the Changes pane is hard-titled 'Uncommitted changes' (a non-default scope in the original). Local base inference also copies resolveCloudBranch (current branch first) instead of getGitInfo defaultBranch.

Base comes from c0547825d session repos: baseBranch = git.defaultBranch ?? sourceBranch ?? branch, with defaultBranch from `symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` else origin/main|master (index.chunk-Mak6MV2t ~5254). Scope picker: panes-tile-current.js:2946-3080 (zm: 'All changes' hint 'vs {base}' default, 'Uncommitted changes', Commits). Local: app/electron/git-status.cjs:276-301 (numstat against ctx.head, hasChanges = porcelain records), 303-312 (workspaceGitDiff vs HEAD), 217-240 (resolveBase copies cloud-branch order), 253 (branch===base short-circuits with no merge-base); app/src/main.jsx:344-345 (commitDisabled = !hasChanges); app/src/source-session.jsx:1480-1483 ('Uncommitted changes' title); main.jsx:2121 diffScope='uncommitted'.
findings.fix: In git-status.cjs, add defaultBase(ctx): `symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` (strip origin/), else the first of main/master that has refs/remotes/origin/<b>, else preferredBase (worktree sourceBranch), else the current branch. Resolve the ref like ua (origin/<b>, then <b>, then HEAD), take mergeBase = `merge-base <ref> HEAD` || ref, and compute numstat and the Changes patch with `git diff ... <mergeBase> --` plus the existing untracked additions. Return hasChanges = files.length > 0, a new workingTreeDirty = porcelain records.length > 0, diffBase = mergeBase and scopeBase = <b>. Keep the comparison()/behind logic, but feed it the same base. In main.jsx:344-345 and git-rail-model.mjs commitAction, gate on workingTreeDirty (reason 'No changes to commit' when clean, 'Claude is working…' when responding). (b) An unpushed commit on main is included. (c) A repo with no remote equals today's HEAD diff. Run `cd app && node --test tests/git-status.test.mjs tests/git-rail-model.test.mjs`. findings.title: Dismiss X is shown in commit mode, where the original never offers one
findings.difference: The original row is dismissable only when the PR lookup answered 'no PR' (z === null), which needs a GitHub repo slug. In commit mode (local session, no GitHub repo) the PR lookup is impossible, so pr stays undefined. onDismiss is then undefined and dismissReserved is false, and the row ends flush with the Commit button. The local band always appends an X. Its dismissal is also a single in-memory session id: dismissing session B re-shows A, a restart re-shows it, and a branch change keeps it hidden. Where dismissal does exist in the original, it is persisted in localStorage 'epitaxy.dismissedPrMap' per session and keyed by repo/cwd + branch.

findings.title: Opening Settings does not put the caret in Search (the original focuses the nav search on open, with no focus ring)
findings.difference: In the original, the Settings modal does not take initial focus itself. Instead, the nav SettingsNavSearch focuses its input on mount, using {preventScroll:true, focusVisible:false}, so after Cmd+, the user can type a query at once. Its field ring only shows on :focus-visible and it has a hover ring. Locally the dialog <section> is focused, so typing does nothing until the user clicks Search or presses Cmd+F. The local ring uses :focus-within, so focusing the input by script would also draw a ring, which the original avoids. The hover ring is missing.

findings.title: No native right-click menu: Cut/Copy/Paste, Look Up, spelling, link and image items are all missing
findings.difference: In the original, right-clicking text or a link opens Electron's native context menu, built by _W from the webContents context-menu params. Groups are separated and appear in this order: dictionary suggestions (replaceMisspelling); Learn Spelling; Look Up (showDefinitionForSelection) when text is selected; for http/https links without credentials, Open Link in Default Browser and Copy Link Address; Copy Image and Copy Image Address; Undo/Redo when the field is editable and canUndo/canRedo; Cut/Copy/Paste with roles and enabled state from editFlags (non-editable text gets Copy only); Select All when canSelectAll; Inspect Element only when allowDevTools is on. Any previous popup is closed first. The local app registers no 'context-menu' listener at all. Right-clicking in the composer, settings inputs, selected transcript text, links or images therefore does nothing; Electron has no default menu. The only right-click menus are the React SourceMenu ones on sidebar rows, file tabs, diff and image components.
findings.evidence: Original: reference/current-2.2553.1/readable/electron-context-menu-excerpt.js:1 (_W menu builder, popup with hostWindow/viewOffset, and the gW single-popup guard). Local: app/electron/main.cjs:302 and :422-424 register only will-navigate and render-process-gone on webContents. Grepping app/electron for 'context-menu', showDefinitionForSelection or replaceMisspelling finds nothing, and app/src has no document-level contextmenu handler.

It should mirror _W's group order, labels ('Learn Spelling', 'Look Up', 'Open Link in Default Browser', 'Copy Link Address', 'Copy Image', 'Copy Image Address', 'Undo', 'Redo', 'Cut', 'Copy', 'Paste', 'Select All', 'Inspect Element'), accelerators, roles and enabled flags, and insert separators only between non-empty groups. In main.cjs createWindow (and any popout window), add win.webContents.on('context-menu', (e, params) => Menu.buildFromTemplate(...).popup({window, x, y})). Close any menu that is still open first. Route Open Link through the existing external-URL path (shell.openExternal, http/https only, no username or password). Existing React menus are unaffected because they call preventDefault on the DOM contextmenu event, so Chromium never asks for a native menu there.

Cover an editable field with canPaste/canUndo (Undo, Redo, sep, Cut, Copy, Paste, sep, Select All), selection-only static text (Look Up, sep, Copy, sep, Select All), an http link versus a javascript: link (Open Link only for http), an image with srcURL, a misspelled word with suggestions, and no Inspect Element unless allowDevTools. findings.title: Appearance: defaults to Light instead of system, flashes light at boot, and never updates nativeTheme or the dark window background
findings.difference: The original stores userThemeMode with default 'auto' (follow system) and starts from html data-mode="system", so CSS media queries paint dark immediately. It sends the mode to Electron (nativeTheme.themeSource), creates windows with backgroundColor #151515 in dark and #fcfcfb in light, and updates the colour on nativeTheme 'updated'. On a mode flip it finishes running colour transitions so the switch is instant. Locally the default is 'light', index.html hard-codes data-mode="light" and React starts with useState("light") until the async boot IPC returns, so dark-mode users see a light frame on every launch and popout. Every BrowserWindow uses a fixed #fcfcfb, which shows as light bands during resize and window creation in dark mode. Native UI (window chrome, native menus, <select> popups) follows the OS rather than the in-app choice. Elements with background/colour transitions animate visibly when the theme changes. In addition, `/theme auto` errors ('Use /theme system…') and an unknown argument throws, where the original treats auto as system and opens the picker for unknown arguments.

findings.title: style.css strips the original font fallback chains (CJK, ui-monospace, metric-matched serif) from --font-anthropic-*
findings.difference: The original defines --font-anthropic-sans as "anthropic-sans", system-ui, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, then the CJK chain (PingFang SC/TC, Hiragino Sans, Apple SD Gothic Neo), then sans-serif. --font-anthropic-serif adds the metric-overridden 'Anthropic Serif Fallback Georgia/Times/DejaVu/Noto' faces, and --font-anthropic-mono adds ui-monospace. The override is unnecessary: all 19 woff2 files referenced by the loaded CSS exist in app/public/assets/v1 (local private copy; app/public/third-party/fonts.txt states Anthropic Sans/Mono are proprietary and not redistributed). plan.overview:
Planner result for the fidelity round. All region findings were triaged into 14 sequential batches; 10 findings are deferred.

Spot-checks (read-only) of doubted high-severity evidence, all CONFIRMED in the current tree:
- Phantom tokens. A scan of app/src/*.css against every --cds-* defined in app/public/assets/v1/*.css and app/src found these undefined names: --cds-focus-color (style.css:57, source-session-actions.css:1), --cds-border-focus (4 files), --cds-text-on-primary (source-sidebar.css:364), --cds-shadow-focus, --cds-fill-ghost-pressed/-active, --cds-radius-card/-chip/-lg/-sm, --cds-duration-fast, --cds-delay-hover, --cds-text-info, --cds-bg-000, --cds-shadow-panel, --cds-keycap-radius and --cds-background-primary. --cds-font-code is set at runtime in main.jsx:921-924, so it is not phantom. The loaded CSS really has .cds-root[data-platform=desktop], [data-mode=system] handling, .rounded-card/.rounded-chip and .shadow-panel-sm/-lg. Both preload woff2 files exist.
- Window and menu. app/electron/main.cjs:896 has `app.on("window-all-closed", () => app.quit())` and no context-menu or activate handler. app-menu.cjs uses the roles editMenu and windowMenu.
- Composer. main.jsx navigate() (~1078-1083) always calls setDraft("") and resetAttachments(). turn/completed (~853) only refreshes, and unread is set only by 'mark-unread'. The global Escape (main.jsx ~999-1005) fans out to every layer and ignores defaultPrevented. source-composer.jsx:452/459/470 disable the pickers while running, and :233 sets disabled = !connected.
- Transcript. highlight-engine.mjs registers 5 grammars. The jump control renders ArrowDown 20 in a 36px circle. The real-app screenshot analysis/batch-20260920/official-fade-middle-028-cu.jpg shows the compact CaretDown chip just above the composer, so the classic branch is right. The transcript is role=log with no onContextMenu.
- Approval card. FileChanges is still used in source-session.jsx:330/629.

Merged duplicates and shared root causes:
- Native context menu: titlebar-window-02 and overlays-native-context-menu.
- Focus ring tokens: overlays-undefined-focus-tokens and tokens-theme-focus-ring-tokens.
- Invisible primary label: overlays-group-dialog-primary-label and tokens-theme-phantom-on-primary.
- One shared CDS Dialog primitive: overlays-dialog-primitive and tokens-theme-dialog-surfaces.
- nativeTheme, window background and traffic lights: titlebar-window-07 and tokens-theme-appearance-plumbing.
- Edit > Find plus the find bar: titlebar-window-03 and transcript-find. Follow the renderer find bar (ZB), not webContents.findInPage.
- Highlight changed words and Hide whitespace changes: panes-diff-word-whitespace-toggles and git-changes-menu-display. Use the client-side gn port, not git -w.
- Branch diff base and scope dropdown, sharing one git-status.cjs scope change: git-diff-scope and panes-changes-scope-picker.
- Legacy code-ui Popover removal, together with the composer folder, branch and env chips: overlays-legacy-popover, home-folder-picker, home-branch-picker and home-env-chip-tooltips.
- sidebar-search-palette: only its minimal part (label 'Search', ⇧⌘K, Go > Search…) is done, with titlebar-window-04. The full palette is deferred.
- composer-mode-menu-accept-edits goes with the approval and harness permission work in B7.

Ordering:
- Tokens and primitives come first: B1 tokens and theme plumbing, B2 dialog, shortcut, Escape and shortcuts dialog, B3 popover and env pickers, B4 Electron window, context menu and menu bar.
- Everyday surfaces follow: B5 composer, B6 transcript rendering, B7 tool cards and approvals, B8 sidebar, B9 home.
- The rest come last: B10 find and feed a11y (after B4 makes the Edit menu explicit), B11 Files pane, B12 git band and Changes, B13 Customize, B14 Settings.

Global rules for every implementer:
- Start only after the concurrent B12 workflow and its regression have finished.
- Re-read the current code before each edit, because line numbers drift between batches.
- Do not touch the B12 surfaces: the 'Thought for Ns' thinking status row, the reasoning/thinking rows, the Plan pane task list and the What's new notes. The one exception is replacing a phantom token if one is still present there.
- Cite the original file:line in code comments.
- Add a HANDOFF.md version entry with its 剩余缺口 per convention.
- Keep light, dark and system modes working.
- Do not add Anthropic-account-only features.
